Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D plus probiotic co-supplementation lowered Beck Depression Inventory scores compared with placebo in women with PCOS.
Sentence: "Vitamin D and probiotic co-supplementation, compared with the placebo, significantly improved beck depression inventory [β (difference in the mean of outcomes measures between treatment groups) - 0.58; 95% CI, - 1.15, - 0.02; P = 0.04], general health questionnaire scores (β - 0.93; 95% CI, - 1.78, - 0.08; P = 0.03) and depression, anxiety and stress scale scores (β - 0.90; 95% CI, - 1.67, - 0.13; P = 0.02)."
Measured as: beck depression inventory score
Population: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome aged 18-40 years
Intervention: 50,000 IU vitamin D every 2 weeks plus 8 × 10^9 CFU/day probiotic for 12 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 60
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation did not change self-rated depression (BDI-II) scores compared with placebo.
Sentence: "Although the intervention led to a higher increase of 25(OH)D levels in the VG than in the PG (treatment difference: + 14 ng/ml; 95% CI 4.86-23.77; p = 0.003), the change in BDI-II scores did not differ (+ 1.3; 95% CI - 2.22 to 4.81; p = 0.466)."
Measured as: BDI-II score
Population: Child and adolescent psychiatric patients with vitamin D deficiency (25(OH)D ≤ 30 nmol/l) and at least mild depression (BDI-II > 13)
Intervention: Vitamin D3 2640 IU/day for 28 days plus treatment as usual
Comparator: Placebo plus treatment as usual
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 113
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are placebo-controlled trials measuring BDI scores, but they differ sharply in population (PCOS women vs deficient depressed adolescent psychiatric patients), intervention (vitamin D plus probiotic for 12 weeks vs vitamin D3 alone daily for 28 days), and baseline status.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["intervention","outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: women with PCOS, baseline not reported vs adolescent psychiatric patients with depression and vitamin D deficiency; also vitamin D + probiotic for 12 weeks vs vitamin D3 alone for 28 days"}
